business_problem: DXC needed to build a production-scale agentic operations platform for managed services where specialized AI agents could coordinate complex enterprise IT workflows while meeting enterprise security, compliance, reliability, and accessibility requirements and reducing friction in design, debugging, and delivery.
solution_summary: DXC built DXC OASIS as an AI-native operations platform for managed services using Anthropic’s Claude during development and architecture design. Engineers used Claude Code plus Opus and Sonnet to turn requirements into code, generate UI mockups from DXC OASIS design components, diagnose failures, and reason through supervisor-versus-sub-agent behavior, interruption handling, and load and security trade-offs. In the deployed platform, DXC OASIS uses a unified data foundation to give specialized AI agents shared context, then orchestrates handoffs among agents such as server administration, ITSM, and observability agents. Incident details and telemetry are pulled into this shared context layer so the appropriate agent can act or delegate, while users consume results through a chat interface. The platform was designed for enterprise security, compliance, reliability, and production-scale IT operations.

solution_components.name: Opus

solution_components.name: Sonnet

solution_components.name: ITSM agent
solution_components.role: It provides incident details to other agents operating within DXC OASIS.

solution_components.name: observability agent
solution_components.role: It supplies telemetry data that other agents use for diagnosis and task execution.

solution_components.name: server administration agent
solution_components.role: It handles delegated infrastructure administration tasks within the multi-agent workflow.

data_flow: Enterprise IT signals, incident details from ITSM, and telemetry from observability systems feed DXC OASIS’s unified data foundation. Supervisor logic uses that shared context to route work to specialized agents such as server administration, which hand off tasks and return results through the platform’s chat interface.
business_outcome: DXC OASIS went live in April 2026 and was already deployed to more than 60 customers. DXC says Claude made OASIS software delivery ten times faster, enabled more than 95% of code generation before human review, and helped the platform achieve strong early operational results across IT use cases.
metrics: more than 95% of code generated by Claude before human review
8–10 mins time to close problems, down from 2–6 days
architecture_clues: The platform uses dozens of specialized AI agents that hand off tasks and share context.
DXC describes a unified data foundation that gives every AI agent the context it needs to act and delegate tasks autonomously.
The coordination layer had to define supervisor and sub-agent boundaries, task routing, interruption handling, and behavior under load.
DXC subjected DXC OASIS to production-style security and reliability testing, including edge cases such as slow responses and agent handoffs.
Early results were reported across 56 IT use cases.
